notes: Anchored corpus for PolyDiff qr-family rediscovery + synthetic regressions.
Witnesses are pinned by SHA-256 ONLY. NO payload bytes appear in this repo.

Anchors cover four canonical qr divergence shapes: detected_text divergence (MEDIUM-HIGH; URL-in-QR phishing surface from iOS Camera URL handler vs ZXing extraction), structured-append index/total divergence (MEDIUM; multi-QR ordering bug class), encoding_charset divergence (MEDIUM; ECI-tagged UTF-8 vs default Shift-JIS), and mode divergence (MEDIUM; kanji-mode ambiguity class).
Per-case `implementations` lists the two wrapper ids the case is designed to disagree on; the diff engine runs ALL declared wrappers and picks up these axes (plus any others that surface).
Per-case `expected_fact_vector_diff` is keyed by axis name; each value is a 2-element array of the two impls' observations (matches the `implementations` ordering).

cases.summary: A QR symbol encoding a URL where the iOS Camera URL handler extracts the URL differently than ZXing. Same symbol, different decoded text — when the SMA hands the decoded text to a link router without validating the originator, a phishing surface opens. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation of the URL-in-QR phishing bug class.
cases.limitations: witness bytes are NOT in this repo; pinned-hash anchor only. The expected fact-vector diff documents the canonical disagreement shape — actual decoder outputs depend on the pinned wrapper versions and on whether the iOS Camera detector is available (the stub returns binary_missing off-device, which the diff engine treats as a parse_error divergence).

cases.summary: A multi-QR structured-append sequence (e.g. a payload split across 3 symbols) where two decoders disagree on the index/total reported for one of the symbols. ZXing and ZBar have historically diverged here. When the SMA concatenates parts in the wrong order, downstream consumers see a corrupted payload. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the structured-append divergence triage rule; multi-QR ordering bugs have been documented in QR-decoder research.

cases.summary: A QR symbol with an ECI (Extended Channel Interpretation) header tagging UTF-8, but a decoder defaulting to Shift-JIS interprets the bytes differently. Same symbol, different decoded text + encoding_charset. Maps to a documented charset-confusion bug class. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the encoding_charset divergence triage rule; ECI vs default-charset interpretation differences have been documented in QR decoder research.

cases.summary: A QR symbol whose data fits both byte and kanji modes; two decoders disagree on which mode was used. Same symbol, different mode + (downstream) different decoded text when the kanji mode is mis-applied to byte data. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the mode divergence triage rule; kanji-mode ambiguity has been documented in QR decoder research.
